answer: Cross-epoch behaviour consistency rule: each identity must reproduce its prior-epoch action distribution within a tolerance band, checked at a fixed vertex in the reputation graph. An identity whose divergence exceeds tolerance is throttled until it re-earns standing through sustained low-divergence epochs across the reef of tracked interactions. Cloned identities must therefore sustain distinct histories rather than copy a template, imposing continuous per-identity maintenance cost on the operator's atlas of accounts.
